facts.text: Norwood was first laid out in 1904 between Fox Street and Namayo Avenue, and between Norwood Boulevard and Alberta Avenue.
The area north of Alberta Avenue was called Alberta Avenue, while the south was Norwood, and the city officially named the whole neighbourhood Alberta Avenue in the 1980s.
Norwood once housed the Great Western Garment Company and the Norwood Foundry, key employers during World War I.
Today, Norwood residents enjoy the nearby Commonwealth Recreation Centre and Sprucewood Library, anchors of the community.
Norwood is experiencing a revival thanks to its close proximity to downtown Edmonton, affordable homes, and easy transit access.
The Alberta Avenue History Project, launched by Rat Creek Press, celebrates Norwood’s rich past with community events and research.
